title: Split a String Into the Max Number of Unique Substrings
summary: Given a string s, determine the greatest number of distinct substrings it can be divided into, ensuring each substring is unique and their concatenation forms the original string.
statement: Given a string s, determine the greatest number of distinct substrings it can be divided into, ensuring each substring is unique and their concatenation forms the original string.
constraints: Split s into non-empty contiguous substrings whose concatenation is s.
Require every chosen substring to be distinct and maximize the number of parts.
hints: Backtrack over every possible next substring boundary.
Choose a part only if it is absent from the current used set, then remove it after recursion.
Record the largest set size at the end of the string.
Every legal split corresponds to one root-to-leaf boundary sequence, and the used set enforces uniqueness exactly.
editorial: Every legal split corresponds to one root-to-leaf boundary sequence, and the used set enforces uniqueness exactly.

tests.explanation: One optimal split is a, b, ab, c, cc, giving five unique parts.
Splitting as a, b, a repeats a, so the best unique split has two parts.
